children: Bond traders are bracing for the release of New Zealand's third quarter inflation data next week to firm up expectations on the next move by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand. An annual inflation rate just shy of 4.0% is expected, which will be enough to keep policymakers on edge, especially amid data elsewhere showing the economy remains on a solid footing. The RBNZ's next policy meeting is on October 28. Sharon Zollner, chief economist at ANZ, remains cautious, saying a weaker New Zealand dollar and higher oil prices since September keep an October interest rate rise firmly on the table.(james.glynn@wsj.com; X @JamesGlynnWSJ)
